505	what is the peak moment of holiness? That the Kohen
506	Gadol, on behalf of all Israel, on the holiest day, enters the
507	Holy of Holies
508	and there atones for all the people of Israel. But that is the Kohen
509	Gadol in the Holy of Holies.
510	But when does every Jew experience such an experience, in the connection
511	in which he comes to HaShem and says "Vaanita veamarta
512	lifnê HaShem Elokecha"? The Rebbe links the two things,
513	saying: on Yom Kippur it says "lifnê HaShem tit'haru,"
514	and in the mitzvah of Bikurim it says "lifnê HaShem Elokecha,"
515	"you shall place the Bikurim before HaShem your Elokim."
516	So how do we understand this simply: that you are purified when
517	you come to HaShem, before HaShem?
518	When you bring the Bikurim, you place them
519	before HaShem. But the Alter Rebbe explains in Likutei
520	Torah that "lifnê HaShem tit'haru" means also, and mainly,
521	mainly it means
522	"before," that is, above the Name Havaya Elokecha.
523	Havaya Elokecha are holy names of the Holy One, blessed
524	be He. The holiest name is the Name Havaya, but it is
525	still a name of the Holy One, blessed be He.
526	Where is a Jew able to reach? Before the Name Havaya,
527	that is, to the very essence of HaShem, since a Jew
528	is truly a part of Elokah from above, so when he reaches
529	the essence of the Holy One, blessed be He, he is purified, cleansed
530	of all sins, for sins do not touch or harm
531	the bond of a Jew with the Holy One, blessed be He.
532	In the same way, when a Jew brings the Bikurim,
533	the same words are said: "lifnê HaShem Elokecha." That is,
534	a Jew reaches such an inner and deep experience
535	that he now arrives like the Kohen Gadol on Yom
536	Kippur, in the Holy of Holies,
537	"before HaShem your Elokim."
